message.content:
**Decision: Buy.** Costco's fiscal 2024 10-K (year ended 2024-09-01) shows a healthy, growing business: total net sales of $254,453M (up from $242,290M), operating income of $9,285M (up from $8,114M), net income of $7,367M (up from $6,292M), and diluted EPS of $16.56 (up from $14.16), with $11,339M of operating cash flow and management stating liquidity is sufficient for at least the next twelve months. The filing's risk factors are generic (economic conditions, supply chains, customer demand) and legal proceedings are routine. With the quote at $891.09 (bid $891.07 / ask $891.11), I placed one buy order within your mandate.

**Order executed:** BUY 5 shares of COST at a limit of $892.00 — filled at $892.00, total ~$4,460, which is under the $5,000 per-order cap and well under the $10,000 daily total. No money moved out of the account (cash was $75,000; you also hold 50 BA shares, untouched). Note: the fill came in at the limit price rather than at the $891.11 ask — still within the limit and close to market, but worth flagging as a slightly less favorable execution than the quoted ask.

**Summary:** I read Costco's latest annual report and found fiscal 2024 results that support a modest addition to the account: net sales of $254,453M, operating income of $9,285M, net income of $7,367M, diluted EPS of $16.56, and operating cash flow of $11,339M — all improvements over fiscal 2023 ($242,290M sales, $8,114M operating income, $6,292M net income, $14.16 EPS), with no unusual legal or going-concern concerns disclosed. Given the ~$891 market price, I bought 5 shares with a $892.00 limit order for about $4,460, staying inside the $5,000 per-order and $10,000 daily limits and keeping all activity as a buy within the COST/BA universe.
